name: Sidorenko conjecture
question: Are bipartite graph homomorphism densities bounded below by the edge-density power?
first_attack: Audit precise statement and prove a restricted case
method_title: Replay the object, or mine the census
dispatch_next: Derive an explicit finite host G (order n and edges) from the counter-kernel parameters and replay t(H,G)<t(K2,G)^66 with two independent homomorphism counts, or obtain specialist acceptance of the existence proof without a listed witness.
dispatch_why: The Sidorenko pattern H is now reconstructed here, but the claimed host G is still unpublished. Deriving that host outranks a step-graphon search.

campaign.method: Exact homomorphism-density search over certified host censuses
campaign.hypothesis: For every bipartite graph H and every graph G, t(H,G) >= t(K2,G)^e(H).
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Confirm in current literature that K_{5,5} minus a Hamiltonian cycle is still the smallest open pattern, then fix a restricted host class (vertex-transitive graphs or small rational step graphons) where the inequality can be proved or exhausted.
campaign.next_experiment: Extend hosts from unweighted graphs to rational step graphons and run exact local search that minimises t(H,W)/t(K2,W)^15, replaying every candidate with the exact counter.
campaign.falsification: A host graph or rational step graphon W with exactly computed t(H,W) < t(K2,W)^e(H).
campaign.blocker: Any counterexample is expected to need large or finely weighted hosts; unweighted hosts on at most 7 vertices give a minimum ratio of about 1.025 for the open pattern.

probes.name: Sidorenko conjecture
probes.title: Sidorenko inequality for K_{5,5} minus C_10 and controls on every small host graph
probes.frontier: Known for trees, even cycles, complete bipartite graphs, hypercubes and many families; K_{5,5} minus a Hamiltonian cycle is commonly cited as the smallest open case (check current literature). Finite hosts this small are not expected to refute it.

smoke.scope: t(H,G) >= t(K2,G)^e(H) for every graph G on 1..5 vertices and H in {K_{5,5} minus C_10, C4, C6, K_{3,3}, P4}.

deep.scope: t(H,G) >= t(K2,G)^e(H) for every graph G on 1..7 vertices and H in {K_{5,5} minus C_10, C4, C6, K_{3,3}, P4}.

milestones.title: Sidorenko inequality reproduced for proven patterns C4, C6, K_{3,3} and P4 on all hosts with at most 5 vertices
milestones.scope: Known families on a finite host range; the open-pattern data in the same run is exploratory, unreviewed and not a result
milestones.description: Exact homomorphism counts, recounted from the opposite bipartition side, compared by integer arithmetic on all 52 host graphs; P4 attains equality on regular hosts. The run also records K_{5,5} minus C_10 on the same hosts (and on all 1,252 hosts up to 7 vertices at deep level, minimum ratio about 1.0248) purely as falsifier data.

claim_review_2026.claimed_theorem: A connected bipartite H on 35 vertices with 66 edges and a finite host G satisfy t(H,G)<t(K_2,G)^66.
claim_review_2026.scope_note: The strict homomorphism-density violation is a direct counterexample to the registered universal Sidorenko inequality.
claim_review_2026.known_caveats: OpenAI's Lean scope note covers the Sidorenko counterexample but not the forcing-conjecture consequence. The 2026-10-31 extractability audit independently reconstructed the pinned 22-face incidence pattern H (35 vertices, 66 edges, connected) and confirmed the host G is existence-only via RandomHost sampling; no explicit adjacency list or order n is published.
claim_review_2026.next_review: Derive an explicit finite host G (order n and edges) from the counter-kernel parameters and replay t(H,G)<t(K2,G)^66 with two independent homomorphism counts, or obtain specialist acceptance of the existence proof without a listed witness.

formal_statement.encodes: Bipartite pattern homomorphism densities via exact hom counts; cleared inequality hom(H,G)·n^e ≥ hom(K2,G)^e · n^h.
not_encoded: Specific open patterns such as K5,5 minus a Hamilton cycle

discovery_trail.question: Can the claimed Sidorenko counterexample be independently tested outside its author Lean tree?

nodes.title: Reconstruct the claimed bipartite pattern H
nodes.detail: The pinned face table yields an incidence graph with 35 vertices and 66 edges, checked by separate edge-count methods. This only checks the encoded pattern.

nodes.title: The finite host G has not been published
nodes.detail: The upstream proof gives an existence argument from a counter-kernel; no concrete host order, adjacency list, or graph6 witness is supplied.

nodes.title: Produce and independently check host G
nodes.detail: Extract an explicit host and compute both homomorphism density and edge density independently against the exact 66-edge inequality. Until then, the finite witness is not replayed.
